Download a file or a folder under CS9_PATH from the same path on the share

Source: R/util_share.R
path_get.Rd

path_get() takes the arguments of path() and downloads that path from the SMB share in cs9::config$share, a file or a folder with all its subfolders. It returns the local path when each remote file exists locally with the remote size.

Usage

path_get(
  ...,
  create_dir = FALSE,
  trailing_slash = FALSE,
  auto = cs9::config$is_auto
)

Arguments

...

Character strings specifying the second level directory and beyond.

create_dir

Logical value indicating whether to create the directory if it doesn't exist. Defaults to FALSE.

trailing_slash

Logical value indicating whether to add a trailing slash to the returned path. Defaults to FALSE.

auto

Logical value indicating whether this is running in automatic mode (uses base directory) or interactive mode (adds "_interactive" subdirectory). Defaults to the current cs9::config$is_auto setting.

Value

The local path from path().

Details

path_get() first lists the path on the share. A folder is listed again, folder by folder, to find every file below it. path_get() creates the local folders, also the empty ones, and sends one get per file. It then compares the size of each local file with the size in that listing.

path_get() stops, with an error that contains the local path, in these cases:

  • The remote path does not exist.

  • A local file is missing, or its size is not the remote size.

  • Any smbclient call reports an NT_STATUS code or a non-zero exit status.

The checks of the path and of the names in path_put() apply here too, before any smbclient call. When cs9::config$share is empty, only the checks of the path apply. path_get() then downloads nothing, does not check the local path, and returns the path.

See also

path_put(), path_ls()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
folder <- cs9::path_get("input", "weather")
} # }
